reason: Start with the warm response by examining how skin blood vessels help release heat.
expectation: I expect the vessels to widen, bringing more blood near the surface and increasing heat loss to the cooler air.

effect: The widened arteriole connects increased skin blood flow to heat transfer into cooler surroundings; I’ll follow the other warm response next.
reaction: The heat arrows make the cooling route clear.
reason: Sweat glands provide another way to oppose warming.
expectation: I expect the warm signals to stimulate sweating, which can cool the skin as sweat evaporates.

reason: Combine sweat with air to follow how it cools the body.
expectation: I expect sweat to evaporate into the air and carry heat away from the skin.

effect: Evaporation completes the warm response, with humidity reducing evaporation and the temperature-driven signals easing as temperature returns toward its earlier range.
reaction: Separating sweat production from evaporation made the cooling mechanism clear.
reason: Explore how skin vessels oppose cooling, contrasting directly with their warm response.
expectation: I expect the vessels to narrow, reducing blood flow near the skin and slowing heat loss.

reaction: The contrast with widened warm-case vessels is clear.
reason: Follow the only available combination to see how muscle helps oppose cooling.

effect: Shivering completes the cold response by producing heat, distinct from the reduced heat loss caused by narrowed skin vessels.
reaction: The contrast between producing and conserving heat is clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following sweat from liquid production to evaporation was most worthwhile: the separate steps and humid-air comparison make clear what actually removes heat.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial sweating result was relatively slight on its own; its purpose became clear in the following evaporation step.

surprise.text: The humid-air comparison added a useful qualification: sweat cools less effectively when less of it evaporates.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the offered combinations made each response's role clear, although compatibility was supplied rather than discovered.

continue.text: Yes. The contrasting heat-loss and heat-production mechanisms made me curious to see another system explained through connected constructions.
